questions.question_text:
Dividing a fraction by $\frac{5}{6}$ gives $\frac{3}{4}$.
What is the fraction?

options.why: Divided $\frac{3}{4}$ by $\frac{5}{6}$ instead of multiplying to undo the division.
Divided $\frac{5}{6}$ by $\frac{3}{4}$ instead of working back from $\frac{3}{4}$.
Added $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{5}{6}$ instead of multiplying to undo the division.

questions.solution_text:
To undo dividing by $\frac{5}{6}$, multiply by it.
$\frac{3}{4}\times\frac{5}{6}$
$=\frac{15}{24}$
$=\frac{5}{8}$
The fraction is $\frac{5}{8}$.

questions.question_text:
Sally has $\dfrac23$ of a whole cake in the fridge.
Robert eats $\dfrac13$ of this piece.
What fraction of the whole cake has Robert eaten?
Choose the number sentence that would solve the word problem.

options.why: Addition does not represent taking one-third of the available cake.
Division reverses the relationship and gives a value larger than the part eaten.
Subtracts fractions instead of finding one-third of the stored piece.

questions.solution_text: Robert eats one-third of the two-thirds of a cake, so the required operation is multiplication: $\dfrac13\times\dfrac23=\dfrac29$.

questions.solution_text:
Convert the mixed numbers: $1\frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{3}$ and $1\frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{4}$.
$\frac{4}{3} \div \frac{5}{4}$
$= \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{4}{5}$
$= \frac{16}{15}$
$= 1\frac{1}{15}$
So the star is $15$.
